title: Matthew Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 17.

questions.question: In Matthew 17, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus took Peter, James, and John up into a high mountain
Moses and Elias appeared talking with Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus took Peter, James, and John up into a high mountain
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:1 states that Jesus took Peter, James, and John up into a high mountain, which is the first event described in the chapter.

questions.question: Who did Jesus take up into the high mountain with Him?
questions.correctAnswer: Peter, James, and John
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:1 states that Jesus took Peter, James, and John up into the high mountain.

questions.question: How long after did Jesus take Peter, James, and John to the mountain?
questions.correctAnswer: After six days
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:1 says, 'And after six days Jesus taketh Peter, James, and John...'

questions.question: What happened to Jesus on the mountain?
options: He was transfigured and his face shone as the sun
questions.correctAnswer: He was transfigured and his face shone as the sun
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:2 states that Jesus was transfigured before them and his face did shine as the sun.

questions.question: What was said about Jesus’ raiment during the transfiguration?
options: His raiment was white as the light
His raiment was covered in dust
questions.correctAnswer: His raiment was white as the light
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:2 says 'his raiment was white as the light.'

questions.question: Who appeared talking with Jesus on the mountain?
questions.correctAnswer: Moses and Elias
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:3 states that Moses and Elias appeared and talked with Jesus.

questions.question: What did Peter suggest doing on the mountain?
questions.correctAnswer: Making three tabernacles
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:4 shows Peter suggesting making three tabernacles, one for Jesus, one for Moses, and one for Elias.

questions.question: What overshadowed them while Peter was speaking?
questions.correctAnswer: A bright cloud
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:5 states 'a bright cloud overshadowed them' while Peter spoke.

questions.question: What did the voice from the cloud say?
options: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him
This is my prophet, listen to his words
This is the chosen one, follow him
This is my servant, obey him
questions.correctAnswer: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:5 records the voice saying, 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.'

questions.question: How did the disciples react to the voice from the cloud?
options: They fell on their face and were sore afraid
questions.correctAnswer: They fell on their face and were sore afraid
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:6 says the disciples fell on their face and were sore afraid when they heard the voice.

questions.question: What did Jesus do to the disciples after they were afraid?
options: Touched them and said, Arise, and be not afraid
Sent them down the mountain alone
questions.correctAnswer: Touched them and said, Arise, and be not afraid
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:7 states that Jesus came and touched them and said, 'Arise, and be not afraid.'

questions.question: When the disciples lifted up their eyes after Jesus touched them, whom did they see?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus only
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:8 says they saw no man save Jesus only.

questions.question: What command did Jesus give the disciples as they came down from the mountain?
options: Tell the vision to no man until the Son of man be risen again
Tell everyone about what they saw immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Tell the vision to no man until the Son of man be risen again
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:9 records Jesus charging the disciples to tell the vision to no man until the Son of man be risen again from the dead.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples were sore afraid when they heard the voice from the cloud.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:6 states that when the disciples heard the voice, they fell on their face and were sore afraid.

questions.question: True or False: Moses and Elias appeared and talked with Jesus during the transfiguration.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:3 clearly says Moses and Elias appeared talking with Jesus.

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Matthew 17:11, what is Elias expected to do when he comes?
questions.correctAnswer: Restore all things
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:11 states that Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things.

questions.question: What does Matthew 17:13 promise will happen if someone understands who Jesus was speaking about in the previous verse?
options: They will understand that He spoke of John the Baptist
They will be filled with the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: They will understand that He spoke of John the Baptist
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:13 shows that the disciples understood Jesus was speaking about John the Baptist as Elias.

questions.question: What condition did the man describe about his son in Matthew 17:15?
options: He is lunatick, sore vexed, and often falls into fire and water
He is deaf and cannot walk
questions.correctAnswer: He is lunatick, sore vexed, and often falls into fire and water
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:15 describes the boy as lunatick, sore vexed, often falling into fire and water.

questions.question: How do verses 17 and 18 in Matthew 17 connect regarding Jesus' reaction and the outcome?
options: Jesus rebuked the devil and the child was cured immediately
Jesus prayed and the child was healed after a day
Jesus sent the disciples to heal the child again
Jesus told the man to have patience
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus rebuked the devil and the child was cured immediately
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:17 shows Jesus' rebuke of the perverse generation and command to bring the child, and verse 18 shows Jesus rebuking the devil and the child being cured immediately.

questions.question: What does Jesus call the generation in Matthew 17:17 when addressing the disciples' inability to heal the boy?
questions.correctAnswer: Faithless and perverse
questions.explanation: In Matthew 17:17, Jesus refers to the generation as faithless and perverse.

questions.question: What was Jesus' instruction to the disciples after the Transfiguration according to Matthew 17:9?
options: Tell the vision to no man until the Son of man is risen again
Preach the vision to all nations immediately
Build three tabernacles on the mountain
Fast and pray for seven days
questions.correctAnswer: Tell the vision to no man until the Son of man is risen again
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:9 records Jesus charging the disciples to keep the vision secret until after His resurrection.

questions.question: Why did the disciples fail to cure the boy according to what is implied in Matthew 17:16-17?
options: Because of their little faith and the perverse generation around them
Because the boy was too sick
Because they did not have the right authority
Because Jesus had not yet prayed
questions.correctAnswer: Because of their little faith and the perverse generation around them
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:17 shows Jesus calling the generation faithless and perverse, implying the disciples’ lack of faith contributed to their failure.

questions.question: How does the arrival of Moses and Elias during the Transfiguration in Matthew 17:3 relate to Jesus' identity?
options: It confirms Jesus as the fulfillment of the Law and the Prophets
It suggests Jesus is a prophet like them
It indicates Jesus will replace them
It shows their disagreement with Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: It confirms Jesus as the fulfillment of the Law and the Prophets
questions.explanation: Moses represents the Law and Elias the Prophets; their appearance with Jesus in Matthew 17:3 confirms His fulfillment of both.

questions.question: What was Peter’s reaction to the Transfiguration in Matthew 17:4, and what does it reveal about his understanding?
options: He wanted to build tabernacles, showing awe but incomplete understanding
He immediately recognized Jesus as the Messiah
He was afraid and wanted to leave
questions.correctAnswer: He wanted to build tabernacles, showing awe but incomplete understanding
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:4 shows Peter suggesting building tabernacles for Jesus, Moses, and Elias, reflecting reverence but misunderstanding the event’s purpose.

questions.question: What does the bright cloud and voice from heaven during the Transfiguration signify in Matthew 17:5?
options: God’s approval of Jesus as His beloved Son
A sign to start a new covenant
A call to build a temple
questions.correctAnswer: God’s approval of Jesus as His beloved Son
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:5 records the voice from the cloud declaring Jesus as the beloved Son, indicating divine approval.

questions.question: How does the healing of the boy in Matthew 17:18 demonstrate the importance of faith and Jesus’ authority?
options: Because Jesus rebuked the devil and the boy was healed instantly, showing His divine power
Because the boy’s family prayed long enough
Because the disciples finally tried harder
Because the boy was brought to the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Because Jesus rebuked the devil and the boy was healed instantly, showing His divine power
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:18 shows Jesus’ direct authority over the devil and immediate healing, emphasizing faith in Him.

questions.question: What practical lesson about prayer and faith can be learned from the father's plea in Matthew 17:15-16?
options: Persistent prayer is necessary even when others cannot help
Only disciples can heal the sick
Faith is not important for miracles
questions.correctAnswer: Persistent prayer is necessary even when others cannot help
questions.explanation: The father’s earnest plea in Matthew 17:15-16, despite the disciples' failure, teaches persistence in prayer and faith.

questions.question: According to Matthew 17:12, what is the analogy Jesus makes about Elias and the Son of man?
options: Elias has come and was rejected, likewise the Son of man will suffer
Elias will come after the Son of man
Both will establish a new kingdom immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Elias has come and was rejected, likewise the Son of man will suffer
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:12 explains that Elias has already come and was rejected, and similarly the Son of man will suffer.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus told His disciples to immediately share the vision of His Transfiguration with everyone they met.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:9 instructs the disciples to tell the vision to no man until after the Son of man rises from the dead.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples were able to heal the boy before bringing him to Jesus.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:16 states the disciples could not cure the boy before Jesus intervened.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 17.

questions.question: Why could the disciples not cast out the devil?
options: Because the devil was too strong
questions.correctAnswer: Because of their unbelief
questions.explanation: Jesus explained that the reason was 'Because of your unbelief' (Matthew 17:20).

questions.question: What did Jesus say could be done with faith as small as a mustard seed?
questions.correctAnswer: Move mountains
questions.explanation: Jesus stated, 'If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove' (Matthew 17:20).

questions.question: What is necessary for casting out the kind of devil mentioned by Jesus?
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer and fasting
questions.explanation: Jesus said, 'Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting' (Matthew 17:21).

questions.question: What did Jesus predict would happen to the Son of man?
options: He will be betrayed and killed
questions.correctAnswer: He will be betrayed and killed
questions.explanation: Jesus said, 'The Son of man shall be betrayed into the hands of men: And they shall kill him' (Matthew 17:22-23).

questions.question: What did Peter say when asked if Jesus pays tribute?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes, he does
questions.explanation: Peter replied, 'Yes' when asked if Jesus pays tribute (Matthew 17:25).

questions.question: What did Jesus instruct Peter to do in order to pay the tribute?
options: Cast a hook into the sea
questions.correctAnswer: Cast a hook into the sea
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed Peter to 'go thou to the sea, and cast an hook' to find the money needed for tribute (Matthew 17:27).

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'πιστις' (pistis) in Matthew 17:20 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Faith
questions.explanation: 'πιστις' (pistis) means 'faith,' referring to the trust and belief needed to perform miracles as stated in Matthew 17:20.

questions.question: What literary technique is primarily used in Matthew 17:20 when Jesus talks about faith as a mustard seed?
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: The comparison of faith to a mustard seed is a metaphor, illustrating that even a small amount of genuine faith can achieve great things (Matthew 17:20).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to Jesus' prediction of his death in Matthew 17:22?
questions.correctAnswer: Luke 9:22
questions.explanation: Luke 9:22 parallels Matthew 17:22, stating, 'The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be slain, and be raised the third day.'

questions.question: Which Old Testament event does the healing of the boy in Matthew 17:18 echo?
questions.correctAnswer: The confrontation with Baal
questions.explanation: The healing of the boy parallels Elijah's confrontation with the prophets of Baal, as both involve deliverance from demonic affliction (1 Kings 18).

questions.question: What comes before Jesus' statement about the mountain in Matthew 17:20?
questions.correctAnswer: The healing of the boy
questions.explanation: Before Jesus' statement in Matthew 17:20, He had just healed a boy possessed by a devil (Matthew 17:18).

questions.question: What does the term 'fasting' in Matthew 17:21 signify?
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual discipline
questions.explanation: Fasting in Matthew 17:21 signifies a spiritual discipline necessary for deeper connection and effectiveness in prayer and spiritual warfare.

questions.question: What does the term 'unbelief' in Matthew 17:20 refer to?
questions.correctAnswer: Doubt in God's power
questions.explanation: 'Unbelief' refers to doubt in God's power and ability to perform miracles, which hindered the disciples from casting out the demon (Matthew 17:20).

questions.question: Jesus' statement about his betrayal in Matthew 17:22 is an example of what?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jesus' prediction about his betrayal is a prophetic statement that fulfills Old Testament prophecy and reveals his mission (Matthew 17:22).

questions.question: The money found in the fish's mouth in Matthew 17:27 was for Peter alone.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The money was for both Peter and Jesus, as stated, 'that take, and give unto them for me and thee' (Matthew 17:27).

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 17:2 teach about the divine nature of Christ?
options: Christ’s divine glory is revealed visibly
Christ’s role as prophet is highlighted
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s divine glory is revealed visibly
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:2 shows Jesus transfigured with a face shining as the sun and garments white as light, revealing His divine glory.

questions.question: What doctrine about prophetic fulfillment does Matthew 17:11 teach?
options: Elijah must come first to restore all things
The Messiah comes without prophetic preparation
John the Baptist is unrelated to Elijah
questions.correctAnswer: Elijah must come first to restore all things
questions.explanation: In Matthew 17:11, Jesus states Elijah will first come to restore all things, affirming fulfillment of prophecy.

questions.question: What doctrine about faith and spiritual authority is taught in Matthew 17:20?
options: Faith, even as a mustard seed, enables impossible works
Only miracles by Jesus are valid
Faith is irrelevant to spiritual power
Unbelief is a sign of true wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Faith, even as a mustard seed, enables impossible works
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:20 teaches that faith as small as a mustard seed can move mountains and enable believers to do all things.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 17:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: In Matthew 17:5, God's voice from the cloud declares Jesus as His beloved Son, showing divine holiness and approval.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by Jesus’ rebuke of the devil in Matthew 17:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:18 demonstrates Jesus’ sovereign authority over demonic powers by rebuking the devil and healing the child.

questions.question: How does the transfiguration event in Matthew 17:1–2 connect to the broader biblical narrative?
options: It prefigures Christ’s glorification after resurrection
It marks the beginning of the Church age
It confirms the abandonment of the Law
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Christ’s glorification after resurrection
questions.explanation: The transfiguration in Matthew 17:1–2 anticipates Christ’s future glorification, connecting to His resurrection and exaltation (Philippians 3:21).

questions.question: In what way does Matthew 17:22–23 prepare for the passion narrative?
options: It foretells the Son of man’s betrayal, death, and resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: It foretells the Son of man’s betrayal, death, and resurrection
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:22–23 explicitly proclaims Jesus’ betrayal, death, and resurrection, preparing the reader for the passion.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 17:3 and 17:5 teach about God’s revelation and Christ’s identity?
options: Christ is affirmed as God’s Son through prophetic witnesses and divine voice
Christ is solely a human prophet
Moses and Elijah replace Jesus as mediators
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is affirmed as God’s Son through prophetic witnesses and divine voice
questions.explanation: Verses 17:3 and 17:5 show Moses and Elijah talking with Jesus and God’s voice affirming Him as Son, confirming His divine identity.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Matthew 17:12 and 17:13 provide about John the Baptist’s role?
options: John the Baptist is the Elijah who was to come first
John the Baptist is unrelated to Old Testament prophecy
John the Baptist was rejected due to his sin
John the Baptist was a political revolutionary
questions.correctAnswer: John the Baptist is the Elijah who was to come first
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:12–13 explains Jesus identifies John the Baptist as the fulfillment of Elijah’s coming, though he was not recognized.

questions.question: What doctrine about spiritual warfare and human responsibility is taught by combining Matthew 17:18 and 17:21?
options: Deliverance requires Jesus’ authority plus prayer and fasting
Faith alone without prayer is sufficient
Humans control demons by their own power
questions.correctAnswer: Deliverance requires Jesus’ authority plus prayer and fasting
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:18 shows Jesus casting out a demon, and 17:21 states that certain kinds of demons require prayer and fasting, combining divine authority with human discipline.

questions.question: Skeptics claim the transfiguration story is a myth with no historical basis. What does Matthew 17:1–9 actually teach about the event?
options: It was a real, witnessed event revealing Jesus’ divine glory
It was a parable about future glory
It was a dream Peter had
It was a later church invention
questions.correctAnswer: It was a real, witnessed event revealing Jesus’ divine glory
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:1–9 records Jesus taking Peter, James, and John up a mountain where He was transfigured before them, indicating a historical revelation of divine glory.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ’s lordship and covenant relationship with Israel is taught in Matthew 17:25–27?
options: Christ, as the Son, is exempt from temple tax but submits to avoid offense
Christ pays temple tax as a sinner
Christ has no relation to Israel’s covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Christ, as the Son, is exempt from temple tax but submits to avoid offense
questions.explanation: Verses 17:25–27 reveal Jesus’ sonship exempts Him from temple tax, yet He complies to prevent offense, showing covenant respect.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God overshadowing the transfiguration scene in Matthew 17:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Majesty
questions.explanation: God’s bright cloud overshadowing the transfiguration in Matthew 17:5 signifies divine majesty and glory manifesting visibly.

questions.question: How does the healing of the lunatic boy in Matthew 17:14–18 illustrate the doctrine of sanctification?
options: Sanctification involves deliverance from evil through faith and divine power
Sanctification is only a future hope
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves deliverance from evil through faith and divine power
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:14–18 shows Jesus delivering the boy from demonic oppression, illustrating sanctification as cleansing and healing by divine power through faith.

questions.question: What doctrinal synthesis about human unbelief and divine patience can be drawn from Matthew 17:17 and 17:20?
options: God is longsuffering with faithless generation but calls for faith
questions.correctAnswer: God is longsuffering with faithless generation but calls for faith
questions.explanation: In 17:17 Jesus laments unbelief, and in 17:20 He teaches faith’s power, showing God’s patience yet demand for faith.
